cleanup.guest: incus --project opute-e2e delete -f e2e-s7 2>/dev/null; runuser -u opute -- env XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/$(id -u opute) systemctl --user stop opute-provider-k3s opute-provider-cloudflare 2>/dev/null; rm -f /home/opute/.config/systemd/user/opute-provider-*.service; rm -rf /home/opute/.config/opute-e2e7 /home/opute/.opute/build-contexts/e2e-s7-v1 /opt/opute-e2e/guest/leakcheck.py; incus storage volume list default -f csv | awk -F, '$1=="image"{print $2}' | xargs -r -I{} incus storage volume delete default image/{}; true

description: A public website from one host-local recipe: providers installed by typed calls, then evidence/m20/minimal-site.recipe.yaml brings a K3s Service up at e2e-<run>.opute.io through a dedicated Cloudflare tunnel, the host fetches it over verified TLS, a second run skips every node, a deleted pod is replaced, no record holds a token, and the teardown recipe removes the CNAME, tunnel and guest.

inputs.agent: the dev VM's production-style system unit opute-bootstrap-mcp.service (Rust 0.4.0 release candidate binary, test identity e2e-devvm-agent, test token)
inputs.hostname: e2e-${RUN}.opute.io, a CNAME the Cloudflare provider creates in the owner's opute.io zone and removes
inputs.k3s: K3s v1.31.8+k3s1, downloaded by the provider; nginx and cloudflared images pulled from public registries
inputs.providers: the release's K3s and Cloudflare provider executables, started as user units by typed calls
inputs.site: evidence/m20/e2e-site, a static page built into an nginx image

requirements.requirement: One typed plan and recipe execution path
requirements.scenario: One host-local recipe run brings a K3s Service up at a public hostname that the host fetches over verified TLS, a second run skips every node, a deleted pod is replaced, and one teardown run removes the CNAME, the tunnel and the guest (goal m20)

pass.matches: recipe node "inner" cannot recursively run run_host_local_recipe

requirements.requirement: A plan node never starts a plan run of its own
requirements.scenario: A recipe that runs another recipe is refused at validation; the providers installed by typed calls first serve the site recipe's nodes (D44)

requirements.requirement: A validation-only node always evaluates its validation
requirements.scenario: guest-address, connector and public each follow an applied node and are satisfied by their validation (D45)
The Cloudflare API token and the tunnel's run token are in no file under the agent's home but the owner's credentials file, in no journal line and in neither run record
The K3s and Cloudflare providers, started as user units and installed by opute.provider.install, publish their tools in the agent's catalog

contractVersion: runtime-recipe.v1
recipeId: com.opute.k3s.managed
recipeVersion: 1.0.0
runtime:
  id: provider-kubernetes
  servingContract: kubernetes.v1
  capabilities: [kubernetes]
activation:
  capability: kubernetes
  servingContract: kubernetes.v1
  inputBindings:
    providerId: providerId
compatibility:
  requiredTools: [get_host_info]
inputs:
  providerId:
    default: com.opute.k3s
    schema: {type: string, const: com.opute.k3s}
  # Provider activation is repeatable. A caller-scoped nonce keeps a fresh
  # activation from replaying a terminal plan that belongs to an older
  # provider generation.
  activationNonce:

    schema: {type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 128}

  contractVersion: host-plan.v1

steps.guest: for i in $(seq 60); do ss -ltnH 'sport = :4320' | grep -q . && break; sleep 0.5; done; ss -ltnH 'sport = :4320' | wc -l

python3 -c 'import sys, time, json; sys.path.insert(0, "/opt/opute-e2e/guest"); import mcpwire
for i in range(120):
    r = mcpwire.mcp(3014, sys.argv[1], "tools/list", request_id=i + 1)
    names = [t["name"] for t in ((r.get("body") or {}).get("result") or {}).get("tools") or []]
    if "opute.capability.kubernetes.provision" in names: break
    time.sleep(0.5)
print(json.dumps({"listed": "opute.capability.kubernetes.provision" in names, "tools": len(names)}))' '${TOKEN}'

arguments.content:
# m20: a static website served from a K3s Service and published at a Cloudflare hostname, brought up by one
# run_host_local_recipe. Every node is a typed tool with a validate on its effect, so a second run finds each
# effect in place and skips every action (status "satisfied").
#
# Host prerequisites, set up once by typed calls before the first run (evidence/m20/README.md): the K3s and
# Cloudflare providers installed with opute.provider.install (an install runs its own activation recipe, which
# a node of this recipe cannot do, D44), and the container builder.
#
# The cluster pulls the image from the in-cluster registry as localhost:30500 (the registry's NodePort on the
# node itself), which containerd reaches over plain HTTP with no registry configuration. The host pushes to
# the same registry at the guest's address.
contractVersion: host-recipe.v1
recipeId: com.opute.host-agent.minimal-site
recipeVersion: 1.0.0
execution:
  coordinator: host-agent
  mode: local
compatibility:
  requiredTools:
    - provision_vm
    - get_vm_info
    - opute.capability.kubernetes.provision
    - opute.capability.kubernetes.status
    - install_oci_registry
    - get_oci_registry_status
    - stage_build_context
    - inspect_host_file
    - build_and_push_oci_image
    - probe_http_endpoint
    - apply_manifest
    - get_cluster_resource_status
    - configure_service_domain
    - get_cluster_resource
    - ensure_cloudflared_tunnel
    - get_cloudflare_tunnel_status
inputs:
  hostname:
    required: true
    description: Public hostname; the provider creates its tunnel route and CNAME.
    schema: {type: string, pattern: '^(minimal|e2e-[a-z0-9-]{1,40})\.opute\.io$'}
  tunnelName:
    required: true
    description: Name of the dedicated Cloudflare tunnel that serves the hostname.
    schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$'}
  name:
    required: true
    description: Name of the guest container and its single-node K3s cluster.
    schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}$'}
  guestImage:
    required: true
    description: Incus image alias for the guest container.
    schema: {type: string, minLength: 1}
  contextDir:
    required: true
    description: Absolute host directory the build context is staged into, one per site version.
    schema: {type: string, pattern: '^/.+$'}
  contextFiles:
    required: true
    description: The site's build context (relative path to file content), with a Dockerfile at its root.
    schema: {type: object, minProperties: 1, additionalProperties: {type: string}, required: [Dockerfile]}
  contextEncoding:
    default: utf8
    schema: {type: string, enum: [utf8, base64]}
  siteVersion:
    required: true
    description: Version of the site image; a new context needs a new version.
    schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{0,40}$'}
  containerPort:
    default: 80
    schema: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 65535}
  k3sVersion:
    default: v1.31.8+k3s1
    schema: {type: string, minLength: 1}
  runNonce:
    default: default
    description: A new value starts a new run with the same inputs; it finds every effect in place and skips.
    schema: {type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 128}
plan:
  contractVersion: host-plan.v1
  planId: com.opute.host-agent.minimal-site
  generation: 1
  idempotencyKey: com.opute.host-agent.minimal-site-${vars.inputs.name}-${vars.inputs.hostname}-${vars.inputs.siteVersion}-${vars.inputs.runNonce}
  defaults:
    timeoutMs: 900000
  # A node reads its effect before acting (preflight) unless a node it depends on was applied in this run. A
  # read of a guest or cluster that does not exist yet is refused, so every node that creates one depends on
  # the node applied just before it: from clean state each runs its action, and on a second run each finds
  # its effect and skips. The teardown removes the staged context, which starts that chain again.
  nodes:
    - id: context
      action:
        tool: stage_build_context
        args: {destDir: '${vars.inputs.contextDir}', files: '${vars.inputs.contextFiles}',
          fileEncoding: '${vars.inputs.contextEncoding}'}
      validate:
        tool: inspect_host_file
        args: {path: '${vars.inputs.contextDir}/Dockerfile'}
        assert:
          - {path: /exists, op: eq, value: true}
    - id: guest
      dependsOn: [context]
      timeoutMs: 600000
      action:
        tool: provision_vm
        args: {name: '${vars.inputs.name}', image: '${vars.inputs.guestImage}', instanceType: container, cpus: 2,
          memory: 4GiB, disk: 20GiB}
      validate:
        tool: get_vm_info
        args: {uri: 'container:local:${vars.inputs.name}', fast: true}
        assert:
          - {path: /status, op: eq, value: running}
    # Validation only: waits for the guest's address, which the image node pushes to.
    - id: guest-address
      dependsOn: [guest]
      validate:
        tool: get_vm_info
        args: {uri: 'container:local:${vars.inputs.name}', fast: true}
        assert:
          - {path: /ipv4/0, op: matches, value: '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'}
        pollIntervalMs: 2000
        timeoutMs: 120000
    - id: cluster
      dependsOn: [guest, guest-address]
      timeoutMs: 1200000
      action:
        tool: opute.capability.kubernetes.provision
        args: {targetUri: 'container:local:${vars.inputs.name}', providerInstanceName: '${vars.inputs.name}',
          instanceType: container, version: '${vars.inputs.k3sVersion}', clusterInit: true}
      validate:
        tool: opute.capability.kubernetes.status
        args: {targetUri: 'cluster:local:${vars.inputs.name}', providerInstanceName: '${vars.inputs.name}',
          instanceType: container}
        assert:
          - {path: /readyNodeCount, op: eq, value: 1}
        pollIntervalMs: 5000
        timeoutMs: 300000
    - id: registry
      dependsOn: [cluster]
      timeoutMs: 600000
      action:
        tool: install_oci_registry
        args: {uri: 'cluster:local:${vars.inputs.name}', image: 'registry:2.8.3', storageSize: 1Gi}
      validate:
        tool: get_oci_registry_status
        args: {uri: 'cluster:local:${vars.inputs.name}'}
        assert:
          - {path: /deployment/status/readyReplicas, op: eq, value: 1}
        pollIntervalMs: 5000
        timeoutMs: 300000
    - id: image
      dependsOn: [registry, context]
      timeoutMs: 1200000
      action:
        tool: build_and_push_oci_image
        args: {contextDir: '${vars.inputs.contextDir}', insecureRegistry: true,
          image: '${nodes.guest-address.output.ipv4.0}:30500/site/${vars.inputs.siteVersion}:latest'}
      # A repository per version: its tag list exists once that version is pushed.
      validate:
        tool: probe_http_endpoint
        args: {endpoint: 'http://${nodes.guest-address.output.ipv4.0}:30500/v2/site/${vars.inputs.siteVersion}/tags/list'}
        assert:
          - {path: /statusCode, op: eq, value: 200}
    - id: workload
      dependsOn: [image]
      timeoutMs: 600000
      action:
        tool: apply_manifest
        args:
          uri: 'cluster:local:${vars.inputs.name}'
          manifest: |
            apiVersion: v1
            kind: Namespace
            metadata:
              name: site
            ---
            apiVersion: apps/v1
            kind: Deployment
            metadata:
              name: site-${vars.inputs.siteVersion}
              namespace: site
            spec:
              replicas: 1
              selector:
                matchLabels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: site, app.kubernetes.io/version: '${vars.inputs.siteVersion}'}
              template:
                metadata:
                  labels: {app.kubernetes.io/name: site, app.kubernetes.io/version: '${vars.inputs.siteVersion}'}
                spec:
                  containers:
                    - name: web
                      image: localhost:30500/site/${vars.inputs.siteVersion}:latest
                      ports: [{name: http, containerPort: ${vars.inputs.containerPort}}]
                      readinessProbe:
                        httpGet: {path: /, port: http}
            ---
            apiVersion: v1
            kind: Service
            metadata:
              name: site
              namespace: site
            spec:
              selector: {app.kubernetes.io/name: site, app.kubernetes.io/version: '${vars.inputs.siteVersion}'}
              ports: [{name: http, port: 80, targetPort: http}]
      # Assertion values are not interpolated, so the version is in the Deployment's name: a new version is a
      # new Deployment, and the Service's selector moves to it.
      validate:
        tool: get_cluster_resource_status
        args: {uri: 'cluster:local:${vars.inputs.name}', resourceKind: Deployment, namespace: site,
          resourceName: 'site-${vars.inputs.siteVersion}'}
        assert:
          - {path: /status, op: eq, value: ready}
        pollIntervalMs: 5000
        timeoutMs: 300000
    - id: domain
      dependsOn: [workload]
      action:
        tool: configure_service_domain
        args: {uri: 'cluster:local:${vars.inputs.name}', namespace: site, ingressName: '${vars.inputs.hostname}', ingressClass: traefik,
          hostname: '${vars.inputs.hostname}', serviceName: site, servicePort: 80}
      validate:
        tool: get_cluster_resource
        args: {uri: 'cluster:local:${vars.inputs.name}', kind: Ingress, namespace: site,
          resourceName: '${vars.inputs.hostname}'}
        assert:
          # The read returns the resource as JSON text; the Ingress is named after the hostname it routes.
          - {path: /json, op: notEmpty}
    # The connector runs in the cluster and sends the public hostname to Traefik, which routes it by the
    # domain's Ingress.
    - id: tunnel
      dependsOn: [domain]
      timeoutMs: 600000
      action:
        tool: ensure_cloudflared_tunnel
        args: &tunnel
          bindingId: site
          hostname: '${vars.inputs.hostname}'
          tunnelName: '${vars.inputs.tunnelName}'
          localTarget: 'http://traefik.kube-system.svc.cluster.local:80'
          placement: kubernetes
          targetUri: 'cluster:local:${vars.inputs.name}'
          manageHostConnector: true
      validate:
        tool: get_cloudflare_tunnel_status
        args: *tunnel
        assert:
          - {path: /routed, op: eq, value: true}
    # Validation only: the connector the tunnel node installed is running.
    - id: connector
      dependsOn: [tunnel]
      validate:
        tool: get_cluster_resource_status
        args: {uri: 'cluster:local:${vars.inputs.name}', resourceKind: Deployment, namespace: cloudflare-connector,
          resourceName: cloudflared}
        assert:
          - {path: /status, op: eq, value: ready}
        pollIntervalMs: 5000
        timeoutMs: 300000
    # Validation only: the public URL answers over TLS the agent verifies.
    - id: public
      dependsOn: [connector]
      validate:
        tool: probe_http_endpoint
        args: {endpoint: 'https://${vars.inputs.hostname}/'}
        assert:
          - {path: /statusCode, op: eq, value: 200}
        pollIntervalMs: 10000
        timeoutMs: 600000

# m20: removes what minimal-site.recipe.yaml made: the tunnel and its CNAME at Cloudflare, then the guest
# container with its cluster, registry, workload and connector. Each node validates the absence it makes, so
# a second run skips every action. Removing the staged context's Dockerfile makes the next site run stage it
# again, so that run applies every node from clean state.
#
# Assertion values are not interpolated, and a read of a removed guest is refused rather than answered, so the
# guest node asserts the guest's absence from list_vms by its literal name. The caller fills in e2e-s7
# with the `name` input, as the www-opute-io deploy script fills in its recipe's expected image.
contractVersion: host-recipe.v1
recipeId: com.opute.host-agent.minimal-site.teardown
recipeVersion: 1.0.0
execution:
  coordinator: host-agent
  mode: local
compatibility:
  requiredTools:
    - opute.capability.tunneling.remove-host-tunnel
    - get_cloudflare_tunnel_status
    - delete_vm
    - list_vms
    - remove_host_file
    - inspect_host_file
inputs:
  hostname:
    required: true
    schema: {type: string, pattern: '^(minimal|e2e-[a-z0-9-]{1,40})\.opute\.io$'}
  tunnelName:
    required: true
    schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$'}
  name:
    required: true
    schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,30}$'}
  contextDir:
    required: true
    schema: {type: string, pattern: '^/.+$'}
  runNonce:
    default: default
    description: A new value starts a new run with the same inputs; it finds every effect in place and skips.
    schema: {type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 128}
plan:
  contractVersion: host-plan.v1
  planId: com.opute.host-agent.minimal-site.teardown
  generation: 1
  idempotencyKey: com.opute.host-agent.minimal-site.teardown-${vars.inputs.name}-${vars.inputs.hostname}-${vars.inputs.runNonce}
  defaults:
    timeoutMs: 600000
  nodes:
    - id: tunnel
      action:
        tool: opute.capability.tunneling.remove-host-tunnel
        args: &tunnel
          bindingId: site
          hostname: '${vars.inputs.hostname}'
          tunnelName: '${vars.inputs.tunnelName}'
          localTarget: 'http://traefik.kube-system.svc.cluster.local:80'
          placement: kubernetes
          targetUri: 'cluster:local:${vars.inputs.name}'
      validate:
        tool: get_cloudflare_tunnel_status
        args: *tunnel
        assert:
          - {path: /routed, op: eq, value: false}
          - {path: /tunnelId, op: empty}
    - id: guest
      dependsOn: [tunnel]
      action:
        tool: delete_vm
        args: {uri: 'container:local:${vars.inputs.name}'}
      validate:
        tool: list_vms
        args: {fast: true}
        assert:
          - path: /vms
            op: all
            assertions:
              - {path: /name, op: ne, value: e2e-s7}
        pollIntervalMs: 2000
        timeoutMs: 120000
    - id: context
      dependsOn: [guest]
      action:
        tool: remove_host_file
        args: {path: '${vars.inputs.contextDir}/Dockerfile', confirm: true}
      validate:
        tool: inspect_host_file
        args: {path: '${vars.inputs.contextDir}/Dockerfile'}
        assert:
          - {path: /exists, op: eq, value: false}

steps.guest: for i in $(seq 90); do n=$(incus --project opute-e2e exec e2e-s7 -- k3s kubectl -n site get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=site -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.status.containerStatuses[0].ready==true)]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}' | grep -v -x '${POD}' | head -1); [ -n "$n" ] && break; sleep 2; done; [ -n "$n" ] && echo replaced
incus --project opute-e2e list -f csv -c n | grep -c -x e2e-s7; true
